by_judge.judge: D K SINGH & S VISHWAJITH SHETTY

narrative:
On October 30, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,572 cases across 72 judges, taking up 1,153 matters for an overall hearing rate of 44.8%. This reflects a notable efficiency gain compared to the previous day (October 29), when the court achieved a 37.7% hearing rate across 2,990 scheduled matters. Today's performance also outpaced earlier recorded sessions on October 16 (40.1%) and October 9 (42.6%).

Individual bench productivity showed substantial variation across the courtrooms. Justice K.S. Hemalekha demonstrated strong clearance, hearing 69 of 90 listed cases (76.7%), while Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar addressed 59 of 86 matters (68.6%) on a primary roster and 34 of 50 (68.0%) on a second list. The division bench comprising Justice D.K. Singh and Justice H. Shanthi Bhushan converted 27 of 29 scheduled matters (93.1%). In contrast, heavily loaded causelists encountered procedural delays; Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard 48 of 163 cases (29.4%), and Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar converted 22 of 120 matters (18.3%).

Procedural progression was led by Orders, which accounted for the highest single volume and converted 463 of 979 cases (47.3%). Admission stages followed with 297 heard out of 638 scheduled (46.6%), and Preliminary Hearings converted 45.3% (136 of 300). Final Hearings recorded the lowest conversion among major stages at 27.0% (107 of 396), though this showed slight improvement over October 29's 22.2% clearance rate.

By case type, Writ Petitions formed the bulk of the docket, converting 378 of 914 scheduled cases (41.4%), up from 34.3% on both October 29 and October 16. Criminal Petitions saw 222 heard out of 495 (44.8%), rising from 34.1% on the prior day. Miscellaneous First Appeals sustained consistent progress at 49.0% (219 of 447), while Regular First Appeals lagged at 28.5% (70 of 246).
